title_en: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
title_zh: 被黑应用程序发出的虚假核警告在乌克兰引发不安，但并未引发恐慌
summary: Many Ukrainians, who have faced years of Russian attacks, did not take the messages seriously and doubted their veracity.
summary_zh: 许多多年来遭受俄罗斯袭击的乌克兰人并没有认真对待这些信息，并怀疑其真实性。
body_en: Ukrainians have grown weary of the relentless alerts blaring from their phones and echoing through their streets, day and night, warning of Russian drones and missiles.

On Sunday night, the system delivered something to make them sit up and take note – a succession of more extreme threats that quickly escalated to impending nuclear strikes, chemical attacks and combat on the streets.
But many in the country did not take them seriously and doubted the veracity of the messages.
Sofia Kochmar, 34, a mother-of-one living in the western city of Lviv, said she was initially concerned but quickly questioned the authenticity of the alerts.
"The first thing I saw was the word 'nuclear' and that made me pretty nervous and scared. So my first thought was that something nuclear was actually flying toward us."
"But then the notification mentioned 'street fighting in Kyiv', and I thought, wait, no, that's impossible."
The alerts included some messages written in Russian, and one included a link to a Telegram channel apparently owned by a hacker group.

Within 15 minutes, Ukraine's Air Force issued a statement saying the alert app had been compromised and clarifying there was no radiation threat. But it took more than an hour to issue "all clear" messages.
Anastasiia Romanytska, a 29-year-old ballerina living in Kyiv, said she does not have the alert app installed but friends forwarded her the warnings.
"My first reaction was, 'Is this some kind of joke?' But then my body reacted as if I was under stress. My heart started racing, and my stomach tightened up."
"Still, somehow I immediately realised that it wasn't something serious. Or maybe I just really wanted to believe that."
There are a number of apps delivering phone notifications of air raid warnings, with maps showing areas under threat, all using the same data as the official government-backed app.

Yevhen Baliutov, a cybersecurity expert at Kyiv School of Economics, told the BBC it was clear to him the Ukrainian alert system was hacked by Russians, saying many Ukrainians had clicked a link included with the alerts leading to a Russian Telegram channel, potentially exposing them to further disinformation, phishing attempts or data breaches.
"This is a war, so it's no surprise that Russia will try to hack, will try to send us fake news, will try to manipulate, and will use that for their propaganda."

While both Russia and Ukraine are widely believed to carry out cyberattacks against one another, the informal language used in the hoax alerts on Sunday pointed to so-called hacktivist groups, which could be aligned to Moscow or Kyiv but are not formally directed by either government.
Baliutov said it was also logical that Ukraine would have responded by launching a cyber-attack on the Russian emergency alert system. Both sides have similar capabilities in cyber warfare, he added.
Kochmar said after the initial concern, Ukrainians quickly turned to joking about the incident.

"All our work group chats immediately blew up. Everyone started messaging each other, discussing what was happening. And what I found fascinating was how quickly we turned the whole thing into a joke."
Although the impact of this incident had been limited, it illustrated the weakness of a crucial system, Baliutov said.

"It's very dangerous for Ukraine and for our people. When developing such applications, we need to consider security from the very beginning, without skipping essential security measures. When millions of people rely on a service, we cannot afford to take shortcuts with security."
body_zh: 乌克兰人已经厌倦了手机中不断发出的警报，以及不分昼夜在街道上回荡的警报，警告俄罗斯无人机和导弹。
周日晚上，该系统发布了一些信息，让他们引起注意——一系列更极端的威胁迅速升级为即将发生的核袭击、化学袭击和街头战斗。
但该国许多人并没有认真对待这些消息，并怀疑这些消息的真实性。
34 岁的索菲亚·科赫马尔 (Sofia Kochmar) 是一位住在西部城市利沃夫的一个孩子的母亲，她说她最初很担心，但很快就质疑警报的真实性。
“我首先看到的是‘核’这个词，这让我非常紧张和害怕。所以我的第一个想法是有核东西实际上正在向我们飞来。”
“但后来通知提到‘基辅街头斗殴’，我想，等等，不，这是不可能的。”
这些警报包括一些用俄语编写的消息，其中一条消息包含一个显然由黑客组织拥有的 Telegram 频道的链接。
15 分钟内，乌克兰空军发表声明称警报应用程序已遭到破坏，并澄清不存在辐射威胁。但花了一个多小时才发出“一切清除”消息。
居住在基辅的 29 岁芭蕾舞演员阿纳斯塔西娅·罗曼尼茨卡 (Anastasiia Romanytska) 表示，她没有安装警报应用程序，但朋友们向她转发了警告。
“我的第一反应是，‘这是开玩笑吗？’但随后我的身体做出反应，就好像我处于压力之下一样。我的心开始狂跳，胃部也紧绷起来。”
“不过，不知何故，我立即意识到这并不是什么严重的事情。或者也许我只是真的想相信这一点。”
有许多应用程序可以发送空袭警报的电话通知，并用地图显示受到威胁的区域，所有应用程序都使用与政府支持的官方应用程序相同的数据。
基辅经济学院网络安全专家叶夫亨·巴利乌托夫 (Yevhen Baliutov) 告诉 BBC，他很清楚乌克兰警报系统遭到了俄罗斯人的黑客攻击，并表示许多乌克兰人点击了警报中包含的指向俄罗斯 Telegram 频道的链接，这可能会让他们面临进一步的虚假信息、网络钓鱼尝试或数据泄露。
“这是一场战争，因此俄罗斯会试图进行黑客攻击、试图向我们发送假新闻、试图操纵并利用这些信息进行宣传也就不足为奇了。”
尽管人们普遍认为俄罗斯和乌克兰都对彼此进行网络攻击，但周日的恶作剧警报中使用的非正式语言指向所谓的黑客行动组织，这些组织可能与莫斯科或基辅结盟，但并未受到两国政府的正式指示。
巴利乌托夫表示，乌克兰的回应也是合乎逻辑的，即对俄罗斯紧急警报系统发起网络攻击。他补充说，双方在网络战方面都有相似的能力。
科赫马尔表示，在最初的担忧之后，乌克兰人很快就开始拿这件事开玩笑。
“我们所有的工作群聊天立即炸开了锅。每个人都开始互相发消息，讨论正在发生的事情。我发现令人着迷的是我们很快就把整件事变成了一个笑话。”
巴利托夫表示，尽管这一事件的影响有限，但它说明了一个关键系统的弱点。
“这对乌克兰和我们的人民来说非常危险。在开发此类应用程序时，我们需要从一开始就考虑安全性，不能跳过基本的安全措施。当数百万人依赖一项服务时，我们不能在安全方面走捷径。”

title_en: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
title_zh: 乌克兰战争停火时间最长后，赫尔松地区再次陷入战斗
summary: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.
summary_zh: 尽管史无前例，但为期六天的休战并没有改变持续不断的战争的更广泛轨迹。
body_en: By Laura Gozzi and Vitaly Shevchenko , Chief analyst, BBC Monitoring
Fighting has resumed in Ukraine's Kherson after a six-day truce brought quiet to the front-line region for the first time in years.

The ceasefire - the longest since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - allowed hundreds of people trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky and its surroundings to be evacuated.

On Monday morning, local authorities confirmed that strikes had resumed, saying Moscow had hit a medical facility in Kherson city centre. They also said a 62-year-old woman and a 73-year-old man were injured when a Russian drone attacked the car they were travelling in.
Ukraine also accused Russian forces of using the humanitarian ceasefire to strengthen their military positions, rotate units and deliver ammunition.

"The enemy used the humanitarian pause to set up their positions," said Ukraine's General Staff, adding they had recorded rotation of Russian units, expansion of anti-drone equipment on the roads, and delivery of ammunition.
The Kremlin appeared to corroborate this when spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was "reasonable to assume that the Ukrainian army also used this period for the necessary regrouping".
"It is a completely standard practice in such situations," he added.
The ceasefire had been brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Both Kyiv and Moscow thanked her repeatedly, though no details of her involvement were shared.

An unusual show of cooperation came from Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets. The pair oversaw the ceasefire, travelled into Oleshky and were filmed speaking to residents together. They publicly thanked each other for their work, often highlighting that no violations of the ceasefire had been observed.
Both Lantratova and Lubinets called for the initiative to be repeated elsewhere, and Ukraine repeatedly said it would be prepared to observe similar ceasefires on a national level too.
But many have questioned whether this will lead to more cooperation and further truces.

In fact, the Kremlin swiftly dismissed the idea even as the ceasefire was under way, calling Oleshky "an isolated case" which would not affect the "settlement process" – a euphemism for the stalled peace talks. "There are no similar plans or initiatives," Peskov reiterated on Monday.
And although last week the guns fell silent in Kherson region, elsewhere in Ukraine Russia's air strikes continued, killing scores of civilians and destroying crucial infrastructure.
The decision to observe an unusually broad and comparatively lengthy ceasefire in and around Oleshky was therefore a notable exception.

The ceasefire's observance appears, at least in part, to have been linked to Melania Trump's reported involvement. By violating the truce, Moscow would have risked undermining its own efforts to cultivate the crucial relationship with her husband, US President Donald Trump.
Some commentators have argued that Trump himself would be interested in presenting the Oleshky ceasefire as a foreign policy achievement scored days before the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
"I totally get why our official representatives need to 'play along' with the US first lady on Oleshky," said Artyom Sheynin, a prominent figure on Russian state TV.
"I understand why it's so important to create a 'success story' ahead of the elections for the US president, whose wife 'achieved a ceasefire' in Oleshky."

Kyiv, too, had its reasons to be fully compliant. Although relations with the US and its president are often fraught, Ukraine continues to rely heavily on US intelligence and US-made Patriot air defence missiles to counter Russian aerial attacks. Ahead of another tough winter of war, continued American support is essential to protect Ukrainian skies from Russia's assaults.
body_zh: 作者：Laura Gozzi 和 Vitaly Shevchenko，BBC 监控首席分析师
为期六天的休战使前线地区多年来首次恢复平静，乌克兰赫尔松的战斗又重新开始。
这次停火是自 2022 年俄罗斯开始全面入侵以来最长的一次停火，使被困在俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城镇奥列什基及其周边地区的数百人得以撤离。
周一早上，地方当局证实罢工已经恢复，称莫斯科袭击了赫尔松市中心的一处医疗设施。他们还表示，一架俄罗斯无人机袭击了一名 62 岁妇女和一名 73 岁男子乘坐的汽车，导致他们受伤。
乌克兰还指责俄罗斯军队利用人道主义停火来加强其军事阵地、轮换部队和运送弹药。
乌克兰总参谋部表示，“敌人利用人道主义停顿来建立阵地”，并补充说，他们记录了俄罗斯部队的轮换、道路上反无人机设备的扩展以及弹药的运送。
克里姆林宫似乎证实了这一点，发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示，“有理由假设乌克兰军队也利用这一时期进行必要的重组”。
“在这种情况下，这是完全标准的做法，”他补充道。
停火是由美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普促成的。基辅和莫斯科都多次感谢她，但没有透露她参与的细节。
俄罗斯人权监察员亚娜·兰特拉托娃和乌克兰人权监察员德米特罗·鲁宾涅茨表现出了不同寻常的合作。两人监督停火，前往奥列什基，并被拍到一起与居民交谈。他们公开感谢彼此的工作，并经常强调没有观察到违反停火的情况。
兰特拉托娃和卢宾涅茨都呼吁在其他地方重复这一举措，乌克兰一再表示，它也准备在国家层面遵守类似的停火协议。
但许多人质疑这是否会带来更多合作和进一步休战。
事实上，即使停火正在进行中，克里姆林宫也迅速驳回了这一想法，称奥列什基是“一个孤立的案件”，不会影响“和解进程”——这是对陷入僵局的和谈的委婉说法。 “没有类似的计划或举措，”佩斯科夫周一重申。
尽管上周赫尔松地区的枪声已平息，但俄罗斯在乌克兰其他地区的空袭仍在继续，造成数十名平民死亡，并摧毁了重要的基础设施。
因此，在奥列什基及其周边地区实行异常广泛和相对较长的停火的决定是一个值得注意的例外。
停火的遵守似乎至少部分与梅拉尼娅·特朗普报道的参与有关。如果违反停火协议，莫斯科将面临破坏其与她的丈夫、美国总统唐纳德·特朗普建立重要关系的努力的风险。
一些评论人士认为，特朗普本人有兴趣在周二美国中期选举前几天提出奥列什基停火协议，这是一项外交政策成就。
“我完全明白为什么我们的官方代表需要在《奥列什基》节目中与美国第一夫人‘配合’，”俄罗斯国家电视台的知名人物阿尔乔姆·谢宁(Artyom Sheynin)说。
“我理解为什么在美国总统选举之前创造一个‘成功故事’如此重要，因为他的妻子在奥列什基‘实现了停火’。”
基辅也有理由完全遵守。尽管与美国及其总统的关系经常令人担忧，但乌克兰仍然严重依赖美国情报和美制爱国者防空导弹来对抗俄罗斯的空袭。在另一个艰难的战争冬天到来之前，美国的持续支持对于保护乌克兰天空免受俄罗斯的攻击至关重要。

title_en: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
title_zh: 数千欧洲军队演练乌克兰和平部署
summary: Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in any offensive operations.
summary_zh: 西方官员强调，派往乌克兰的任何部队都不会参加任何进攻行动。
body_en: Britain and France are to lead a military exercise to test a multinational force's ability to deploy to Ukraine, if there is a peace deal.
Nearly 3,000 military personnel from 12 European nations will take part in the rehearsal in neighbouring Poland this month.
Plans for a reassurance force for Ukraine were set out last year as one of the long-term security guarantees being proposed by European nations.

But there are still more questions than answers as to how such a military force might work in practice. Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in offensive operations or be involved in peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring missions.
Nor would they be operating under the command of Nato or on the front line.
Officials say their presence would be to provide reassurance to Ukraine and to help rebuild its armed forces.
The US has been involved in discussions, but is not contributing to the mission.
Russia has already voiced opposition to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine and, last year, President Vladimir Putin said they would be "legitimate targets".
Western officials have declined to spell out the rules of engagement if any international troops were to be attacked in Ukraine. Though they say the force would be able to defend itself.
UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the exercise showed Britain, France and their allies were stepping up preparation for the day when peace came to Ukraine.
He said: "This is not a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops."

Lt Gen Tom Bateman, the UK commander of the Multi National Force – Ukraine (MNF-U), said the exercise represented an important step in translating political commitments into credible military readiness.
He said it was a "real, capable, readily deployable force that represented a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine's long-term stability and security".

Exercise Koalicja - which takes place from 9-22 November - will be a rehearsal of how to move, protect and supply a force in Ukraine. It will also be a test of their command and control to ensure troops from different countries can work together.
Some 2,800 military personnel will take part across land, sea and air, with the UK contribution including 300 troops and a pair of RAF Typhoons.
Fighter jets will simulate how they would reassure commercial aircraft once Ukraine's skies can be reopened.
Turkey has agreed to lead the maritime mission, with the eventual goal to clear mines and allow the resumption of trade in the Black Sea.
As well as the UK, troops will come from France, Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Sweden, and Turkey.
However, Western officials could not comment on the final make-up and shape of the force that could be deployed to Ukraine if the fighting stops.
In the past, military experts have suggested that Western nations might have to send tens of thousands of troops to Ukraine to guarantee its security.
body_zh: 英国和法国将主导一次军事演习，以测试在达成和平协议的情况下向乌克兰部署多国部队的能力。
来自12个欧洲国家的近3000名军事人员将于本月参加在邻国波兰举行的演习。
去年，欧洲国家提出了建立乌克兰安全保证部队的计划，作为长期安全保障之一。
但对于这样一支军事力量如何在实践中发挥作用，问题仍然多于答案。西方官员强调，派往乌克兰的任何部队都不会参加进攻行动，也不会参与维和或停火监督任务。
他们也不会在北约的指挥下或在前线行动。
官员们表示，他们的存在将为乌克兰提供保证并帮助重建其武装部队。
美国一直参与讨论，但没有为这一使命做出贡献。
俄罗斯已经表示反对外国军队驻扎在乌克兰，去年，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，他们将成为“合法目标”。
西方官员拒绝详细说明如果任何国际部队在乌克兰遭到袭击的交战规则。尽管他们说这支部队有能力自卫。
英国国防部长韦斯·斯特里廷表示，这次演习表明英国、法国及其盟友正在加紧准备，迎接乌克兰和平到来的那一天。
他说：“这不是一个假设的计划，而是一支真正的力量，准备在战斗停止后帮助乌克兰。”
英国驻乌克兰多国部队（MNF-U）指挥官汤姆·贝特曼中将表示，这次演习是将政治承诺转化为可靠的军事准备的重要一步。
他说，这是一支“真正的、有能力的、易于部署的部队，代表了自愿国家联盟对乌克兰长期稳定和安全的严肃承诺”。
Koalicja演习于11月9日至22日举行，将演练如何在乌克兰调动、保护和补给部队。这也将是对他们的指挥和控制的考验，以确保来自不同国家的部队能够协同工作。
约 2,800 名军事人员将穿越陆地、海上和空中参加此次演习，其中英国将派出 300 名士兵和两架英国皇家空军台风战机。
一旦乌克兰的天空重新开放，战斗机将模拟如何让商用飞机放心。
土耳其已同意领导此次海上任务，最终目标是清除地雷并恢复黑海贸易。
除英国外，部队还将来自法国、比利时、爱沙尼亚、法国、德国、立陶宛、荷兰、波兰、西班牙、瑞典和土耳其。
然而，西方官员无法对战斗停止后可能部署到乌克兰的部队的最终组成和形式发表评论。
过去，军事专家曾建议西方国家可能必须向乌克兰派遣数万军队以保证其安全。

title_en: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
title_zh: 俄罗斯和乌克兰临时停火期间数百人撤离城市
summary: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.
summary_zh: 俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市的停火已经结束。停火持续了几天，数百名居民得以撤离。
body_en: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine : NPR

Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.
Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.

A ceasefire brokered by Pope Leo and Melania Trump in a corner of southern Ukraine has ended. The truce enabled the evacuation of hundreds of residents in a Russian-occupied town, and across the river in the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, the truce also allowed residents to walk the streets without being targeted by Russian drones. NPR's Joanna Kakissis traveled there this weekend and is on the line from Kyiv. Good morning, Joanna.
JOANNA KAKISSIS, BYLINE: Good morning, Leila.

KAKISSIS: Well, Leila, tunnels of heavy-duty nets cover nearly every street and many of the buildings in Kherson, if you can imagine that. These nets help protect residents from drones because for the last couple of years, Russian soldiers have used FPV, or first-person view drones strapped with explosives, to actually hunt and kill civilians in Kherson. So Russian troops are also about a mile away across a river. They also drop a lot of guided air bombs into the city.

Now, this is a city I first visited in late 2022, right after Ukrainian forces freed Kherson from Russian occupation. Last time I was there was about a year ago. It's a lovely city filled with parks, but, you know, Russian forces have destroyed so many buildings there, and people never left their homes while I was there last time without drone detectors and sometimes even body armor.
FADEL: So how much has changed since you were last there, especially given there was a ceasefire this weekend?
KAKISSIS: Well, Leila, the locals were not wearing body armor this time, and the city did show signs of normal life.

KAKISSIS: We saw people strolling outside with their kids, stocking up on groceries, having coffee in the sun. And at one very busy cafe, we met two best friends, Anna Hersomenko (ph) and Olena Soboleva (ph). They are 21 years old, and here's Olena.
OLENA SOBOLEVA: There is no drones. There is no explosions. It is like a feeling that no one wants to kill you.
KAKISSIS: And Anna told us she took the opportunity to walk to a salon.
ANNA HERSOMENKO: Last two days, I did my nails. Paint my nail. Yeah.
HERSOMENKO: Yes. Thank you a million. Really, it's definitely a lot of people now walking around. A lot of cars.
KAKISSIS: Now, these two friends, Leila, live on the same street, but they only see each other in person about once a month because it's usually so dangerous to walk outside.

FADEL: Wow. So a little bit of a respite for them. So Kherson relaxed a little during the ceasefire, as you pointed out. This truce, though, was negotiated to help a town across the river. What happened there?

KAKISSIS: Well, yeah, Russia and Ukraine agreed to the ceasefire to help the town of Oleshky. This town is occupied by Russian forces, which mined the land around it. Trucks delivering food and medicine could not get in for several months. Some residents in Oleshky were eating boiled weeds to survive. Now, during the ceasefire, hundreds of residents were evacuated from the town, and many went to northern Ukraine to meet their families.
FADEL: Now, the truce ended Sunday night. So does that mean back to war for everyone?
body_zh: 俄罗斯和乌克兰临时停火期间数百人撤离城市：NPR
俄罗斯和乌克兰临时停火期间数百人撤离城市 俄罗斯占领的乌克兰一座城市的停火已经结束。停火持续了几天，数百名居民得以撤离。
俄罗斯和乌克兰临时停火期间数百人撤离城市
俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市的停火已经结束。停火持续了几天，数百名居民得以撤离。
由教皇利奥和梅拉尼娅·特朗普斡旋在乌克兰南部一角达成的停火协议已经结束。停战协议使俄罗斯占领的一个城镇的数百名居民得以疏散，而在河对岸的乌克兰控制的赫尔松市，停战协议还允许居民在街道上行走而不会成为俄罗斯无人机的目标。 NPR 的乔安娜·卡基西斯 (Joanna Kakissis) 本周末从基辅前往那里。早上好，乔安娜。
乔安娜·卡基西斯连线：早上好，莱拉。
卡基西斯：好吧，莱拉，重型网的隧道几乎覆盖了赫尔松的每条街道和许多建筑物，如果你能想象的话。这些网有助于保护居民免受无人机袭击，因为在过去的几年里，俄罗斯士兵使用 FPV（第一人称视角无人机）绑着炸药，在赫尔松实际猎杀平民。因此，俄罗斯军队也在大约一英里外的河对岸。他们还向城市投掷了大量制导炸弹。
现在，这是我在 2022 年底首次访问的城市，当时乌克兰军队将赫尔松从俄罗斯占领下解放出来。我上次去那里是大约一年前。这是一个充满公园的可爱城市，但是，你知道，俄罗斯军队摧毁了那里的许多建筑物，当我上次在那里时，人们从未离开过自己的家，没有无人机探测器，有时甚至没有防弹衣。
FADEL：那么，自您上次访问以来发生了多少变化，特别是考虑到本周末停火了？
卡基西斯：嗯，莱拉，这次当地人没有穿防弹衣，这座城市确实表现出了正常生活的迹象。
卡基西斯：我们看到人们带着孩子在外面散步，购买杂货，在阳光下喝咖啡。在一家非常繁忙的咖啡馆，我们遇到了两位最好的朋友，安娜·赫索缅科（Anna Hersomenko）（博士）和奥莱娜·索博列娃（Olena Soboleva）（博士）。他们今年 21 岁，这是奥琳娜。
奥琳娜·索博列娃：没有无人机。没有爆炸。这就像一种没有人想杀你的感觉。
卡基西斯：安娜告诉我们她借此机会步行去了一家沙龙。
安娜·赫索门科：过去两天，我做了指甲。画我的指甲。是的。
赫尔索门科：是的。谢谢你一百万。确实，现在肯定有很多人在四处走动。很多车。
卡基西斯：现在，莱拉这两个朋友住在同一条街上，但他们大约每月只见面一次，因为外面走路通常很危险。
法德尔：哇。所以给他们一点喘息的机会。正如你所指出的，赫尔松在停火期间放松了一些。不过，这次休战是为了帮助河对岸的一个城镇而谈判的。那里发生了什么？
卡基西斯：嗯，是的，俄罗斯和乌克兰同意停火以帮助奥列什基镇。这个城镇被俄罗斯军队占领，并在其周围的土地上埋设了地雷。运送食品和药品的卡车几个月都无法进入。奥列什基的一些居民靠吃煮熟的杂草来生存。现在，在停火期间，数百名居民从该镇撤离，许多人前往乌克兰北部与家人团聚。
法德尔：现在，停战协议于周日晚上结束。那么这是否意味着每个人都会回到战争呢？

title_en: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
title_zh: 基辅称，俄罗斯轰炸导致乌克兰援助中心26人死亡
summary: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.
summary_zh: 官员们表示，至少有九枚 3000 公斤重的空投炸弹袭击了乌克兰南部的一个村庄，总统称这是一次“极其可怕”的袭击。
body_en: Russian bombing kills 26 people at humanitarian aid centre in Ukraine, Kyiv says - BBC News
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".

Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.
He posted a video showing a huge crater left after Monday's attack, and rescuer teams searching through the rubble.
The Russian military has not publicly commented.
Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.
In his video address late on Monday, Zelensky said 26 people were now known to have died.
He earlier said that "the Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week" on Monday.
"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."

He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky during a temporary ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".
"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.
Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".
He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.
A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Teams from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume peace talks in the next few days after negotiations were suspended in February, with Moscow stepping up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.
However, no major breakthrough is expected at the talks that are likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates.

body_zh: 基辅称，俄罗斯轰炸导致乌克兰人道主义援助中心 26 人死亡 -_澳门赌博平台
俄罗斯炸弹袭击了一个援助物资分发中心，造成至少 26 人死亡，乌克兰领导人称这次袭击“极其可怕”。
地区负责人米哈伊洛·塞米金 (Mykhailo Semikin) 表示，至少 9 枚 3000 公斤重的空投炸弹袭击了扎波罗热州南部地区的 Komyshuvakha 村，造成 5 人受伤，27 人初步报告失踪。
总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基表示，在当地“用于人道主义需求”的学校遭受第一次袭击之后，人们避难的地方又发生了第二次袭击。
他发布了一段视频，显示周一袭击后留下一个巨大的弹坑，救援人员正在废墟中搜寻。
俄罗斯军方尚未公开发表评论。
泽伦斯基最初称死亡人数为18人，但乌克兰国家紧急服务机构DSNS后来表示，确认有24人死亡，其中包括两名救援人员和四名警察。
泽伦斯基在周一晚间的视频讲话中表示，目前已知有 26 人死亡。
他早些时候表示，“俄罗斯人不可能不知道，留在科梅舒瓦哈的当地居民每周都会在那里接受人道主义援助”。
“这再次证明俄罗斯不希望局势缓和。”
他说，在美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普斡旋的临时停火期间，俄罗斯和乌克兰最近成功从俄罗斯占领的南部城市奥列什基撤离平民，“有那么一刻，下一步行动可能表明和平是可能的”。
泽连斯基说：“通过此类杀戮，俄罗斯发出了完全相反的信号——俄罗斯指望进一步杀戮。”
与此同时，塞米金将俄罗斯的袭击描述为该村庄的一场“可怕的悲剧”，并证实“人们仍然在废墟下”。
他说，救援队正在现场开展工作，但由于俄罗斯无人机袭击该地区，他们多次被迫停止行动。
整个扎波罗热地区宣布周二为哀悼日。
俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京于2022年2月对乌克兰发动全面入侵。
乌克兰、俄罗斯和美国的谈判在二月份暂停后，预计将在未来几天内恢复和平谈判，莫斯科加大了攻击力度，因为基辅几乎耗尽了西方提供的拦截导弹。
然而，预计在阿联酋阿布扎比举行的会谈不会取得重大突破。

title_en: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
title_zh: 七个欧洲国家的商店冰柜遭受网络攻击
summary: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
summary_zh: 据报道，欧洲多家商店的冰柜温度高达 50 摄氏度。
body_en: Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers.
Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets.
Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away in October, local media reported at the time.

Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network".

He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates.
Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely.
"The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added.
The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F).
It is unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.

In the US, authorities are investigating what caused refrigeration malfunctions at a number of American military bases in August and working together with French officials to examine whether the incidents could be linked.
Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK.
In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce.
The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.
Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open.
A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

Sweden's budget furniture retailer Ikea said refrigeration systems of its store in the western Belgian city of Mons were affected, with a spokesman quoted by Reuters as saying "we cannot rule out that additional locations may be affected".
In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit.
A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network".
body_zh: 七个欧洲国家的数十家超市遭受网络攻击，其冰箱和冰柜受到影响。
比利时和卢森堡约 40 家德尔海兹超市受到影响，瑞典、爱尔兰、荷兰、爱沙尼亚和芬兰的商店数量较少。
生产部分受影响冰箱的比利时公司 Sabcobel 表示，这些冰箱的蒸发器已切换至除霜模式，导致冰箱升温，据信与上个月袭击数百家法国超市的事件中使用的方法相同。
据当地媒体当时报道，十月份价值数百万欧元的食物不得不被扔掉。
运营德尔海兹系统的 Sabcobel 首席执行官斯蒂芬·莫兰斯 (Stephan Moelans) 周一告诉比利时通讯社，此次事件是一次网络攻击，该公司“整夜工作以断开受影响设备的网络连接”。
他表示，自 10 月初法国袭击事件以来，该公司一直在努力“保护我们客户的冰箱免受此漏洞的影响”，但这些设备需要进行物理修改，而不仅仅是软件更新。
欧洲大多数超市都连接到互联网，维护和故障排除可以远程完成。
“最简单的解决方案是通过安全的互联网连接来管理冰箱。在法国发生袭击事件后，我们的大多数客户都转向了这种方式，”莫兰斯补充道。
据报道，欧洲多家商店的冰柜温度高达 50 摄氏度（122 华氏度）。
目前还不清楚谁是最近一次明显袭击的幕后黑手。
在美国，当局正在调查 8 月份美国多个军事基地出现制冷故障的原因，并与法国官员合作调查这些事件是否存在关联。
比利时和瑞典的国家网络安全机构均表示正在监控这一事件。
英国国家网络安全中心表示，正在与国际合作伙伴和业界合作，“充分了解事件的细节”。英国尚未报告发生任何事件。
在比利时北部佛兰德斯，Hoeilaart 的一家德尔海兹分公司告诉新闻网站 Het Laatste Nieuws，它损失了价值 100,000 欧元（83,500 英镑）的农产品。
该经理表示，这一估计甚至没有考虑关闭商店可能造成的进一步损失。
法资超市家乐福表示，此次事件仅影响其比利时 15 家门店，并补充说已立即采取措施确保所有商店保持营业。
Colruyt 集团以特许经营方式在比利时经营 Spar 商店，其发言人告诉路透社，有 5 家商店的冰箱系统遭到攻击。
瑞典廉价家具零售商宜家表示，其位于比利时西部城市蒙斯的商店的制冷系统受到了影响，路透社援引发言人的话说“我们不能排除其他地点可能受到影响”。
在瑞典，数家 ICA 和 Coop 商店遭到袭击。
ICA 发言人证实，该事件影响了“少数在 ICA 中央网络之外运营的 ICA 商店”。

title_en: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
title_zh: 荷兰警方悬赏200万欧元创纪录追捕毒枭
summary: Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone.
summary_zh: 乔斯·莱德克斯因走私可卡因缺席被判有罪，据信身在塞拉利昂。
body_en: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord Jos Leijdekkers - BBC News
Dutch authorities have offered a record award of €2m (£1.7m/$2.24m) for information leading to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, one of Europe's most-wanted men.
The 35-year-old, who is also known as Bolle Jos (Chubby Jos), was previously accused of being "one of the key players in international cocaine trafficking" by Dutch police.

Commenting on the decision to increase the reward ten-fold, Dutch justice minister David van Weel said it was "necessary given the threat that Leijdekkers poses to national security, our democratic rule of law, and the international legal order".
Dutch prosecutors said capturing Leijdekkers was their "highest priority" and any information shared would be kept secret.
He is listed by Europol, the EU's law enforcement agency, as among their most-wanted fugitives.
In January 2025, Dutch police said he was believed to be living in Sierra Leone and going by the name Omar Sherrif.
Images apparently showing Leijdekkers in the company of President Julius Maada Bio and other officials have previously emerged.
Dutch prosecutors have demanded his extradition but Sierra Leone has refused to cooperate, prompting the EU to cut some aid to the country.
West Africa is a major transit point for cocaine trafficking from Latin America.
In 2024, a court in Rotterdam sentenced Leijdekkers in absentia to 24 years in prison after finding him guilty of smuggling ⁠more than seven metric tons of cocaine.
Several other police investigations in the Netherlands are ongoing.
Leijdekkers has also been sentenced to 79 years in prison in Belgium.
Dutch authorities estimate he has made tens of millions of euros from ⁠cocaine smuggling, and accuse him of money laundering and involvement in the use of extreme violence.
Wanted Dutch drug-smuggler 'is in Sierra Leone'
body_zh: 荷兰警方悬赏创纪录的 200 万欧元追捕毒枭 Jos Leijdekkers - BBC 新闻
荷兰当局悬赏 200 万欧元（170 万英镑/224 万美元），奖励逮捕欧洲头号通缉犯之一乔斯·莱德克斯 (Jos Leijdekkers) 的信息。
这名35岁的男子又名博勒·乔斯（Chubby Jos），此前被荷兰警方指控为“国际可卡因贩运的关键人物之一”。
荷兰司法部长戴维·范韦尔在评论将悬赏金增加十倍的决定时表示，“鉴于莱德克斯对国家安全、我们的民主法治和国际法律秩序构成的威胁，这是必要的”。
荷兰检察官表示，抓获莱德克斯是他们的“首要任务”，任何分享的信息都将保密。
他被欧盟执法机构欧洲刑警组织列为头号通缉逃犯之一。
2025 年 1 月，荷兰警方表示，据信他住在塞拉利昂，名叫奥马尔·谢里夫。
此前曾有图片显示莱德克斯在总统朱利叶斯·马达·比奥和其他官员的陪伴下。
荷兰检察官要求引渡他，但塞拉利昂拒绝合作，促使欧盟削减了对该国的部分援助。
西非是拉丁美洲可卡因贩运的主要中转站。
2024 年，鹿特丹一家法院认定莱德克斯走私超过 7 吨可卡因罪名成立，缺席判处他 24 年监禁。
荷兰警方的其他几项调查正在进行中。
Leijdekkers 也在比利时被判处 79 年监禁。
荷兰当局估计他通过可卡因走私赚取了数千万欧元，并指控他洗钱和参与使用极端暴力。

summary_zh: 对荒龙骨骼进行的化学测试发现了血红素的存在，血红素是一种有机化合物，可以让血液中的血红蛋白将氧气输送到全身。
body_en: Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists | Palaeontology
Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists
Chemical tests on Aratasaurus bone identify presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around body

It could be the opening of a Jurassic Park rip-off: scientists examining ancient dinosaur bones find what appear to be fossilised red blood cells, and traces of the molecule that gives the beast’s blood its distinctive crimson hue.

But that is what researchers are claiming to have discovered after analysing the hind leg bones of a small, meat-eating dinosaur called an Aratasaurus that lived and died in what is now north-eastern Brazil 115m years ago.

Electron microscope images of the dinosaur bones revealed small, round structures that resemble red blood cells in fine channels where blood vessels once ran, while chemical tests identified the presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around the body.

Such claims are controversial because biological tissues and molecules can break down fast, leaving little or no trace in ancient fossils. But if confirmed, it would open up entirely new avenues for scientists, allowing them to investigate dinosaur blood, metabolism and even their activity levels.

“We are seeing a mineral and molecular echo of the dinosaur’s original biology,” said Prof Kliti Grice at Curtin University in Western Australia who led the research team. “Fossilised red blood cells with distinct chemistry related to heme have never been found in situ in any fossil, let alone a dinosaur. This is a world first.”

The fossilised remnants of the Aratasaurus were discovered in a mine in 2008 and have since been held in the National Museum of Brazil, where researchers continue to study them. While analysing the dinosaur’s hind leg bones, Grice spotted the structures that resembled red blood cells.

The scientists’ suspicions that they were looking at red blood cells were bolstered when chemical tests came back positive for heme and its breakdown products. Tests also found traces of the amino acid building blocks for collagen, a key protein in connective and other tissues.

If the structures really are fossilised red blood cells, as the researchers contend, it raises the question of how they were preserved. According to Grice, a manganese compound called hausmannite, which formed in and around the blood cells, may have lent a helping hand by stabilising them prior to fossilisation. The same process might have helped preserve the amino acids, she added. The study appears in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences .

The work is already stoking debate. Prof Mary Schweitzer at North Carolina State University in the US, who has discovered remnants of blood vessels and soft tissues in dinosaur fossils, is not convinced Grice and her colleagues have found red blood cells. One reason for her doubt is that the dinosaur’s red blood cells should have a “nuclear bulge” making them appear dome-like on both sides. The structures Grice found are concave, suggesting they might be something else.

Schweitzer was more persuaded by the discovery of heme and collagen amino acids in the bone and said there was so much more to learn from exceptionally well-preserved fossils. Schweitzer added: “The conventional wisdom in palaeontology that all endogenous organics would disappear in a million years or less is being routinely challenged, and will continue to be as technological approaches to palaeontological specimens are more routinely applied.”

Another question the research raises is what other biological material might lurk in fossils collections around the world. On this, Grice urges extreme caution, adding that her work does not imply that large biological molecules such as proteins or DNA live on in ancient fossils. “Any extraordinary claim needs extraordinary analytical evidence,” she said. “The aim isn’t to find Jurassic Park DNA, it’s to determine how much genuine molecular information deep time can preserve.”

“The really exciting implication is that extraordinary molecular information may already be sitting in museum collections around the world, waiting for us to ask new questions of old fossils,” she added.
body_zh: 科学家称，在 1.15 亿年前的恐龙骨头中发现了红细胞化石古生物学
科学家称，在 1.15 亿年前的恐龙骨头中发现了红细胞化石
对荒龙骨骼进行的化学测试发现了血红素的存在，血红素是一种有机化合物，可以让血液中的血红蛋白将氧气输送到全身
这可能是侏罗纪公园盗版的开始：科学家们在检查古代恐龙骨骼时发现了似乎是化石的红细胞，以及赋予恐龙血液独特深红色调的分子痕迹。
但这是研究人员声称在分析一种名为阿拉塔龙的小型食肉恐龙的后腿骨后发现的，这种恐龙于 1.15 亿年前生活和死亡于现在的巴西东北部。
恐龙骨骼的电子显微镜图像显示出微小的圆形结构，类似于血管曾经运行的细通道中的红细胞，而化学测试发现了血红素的存在，血红素是一种允许血液中的血红蛋白将氧气携带到全身的有机化合物。
这种说法是有争议的，因为生物组织和分子可以快速分解，在古代化石中留下很少或根本没有痕迹。但如果得到证实，它将为科学家开辟全新的途径，使他们能够研究恐龙的血液、新陈代谢甚至活动水平。
“我们看到了恐龙原始生物学的矿物和分子回声，”领导该研究小组的西澳大利亚科廷大学克利蒂·格赖斯教授说。 “从未在任何化石中原位发现过具有与血红素相关的独特化学成分的红细胞化石，更不用说恐龙了。这是世界首例。”
阿拉塔龙的化石残骸于 2008 年在一个矿井中被发现，此后一直保存在巴西国家博物馆，研究人员继续在那里研究它们。在分析恐龙的后腿骨骼时，格赖斯发现了类似于红细胞的结构。
当化学测试结果显示血红素及其分解产物呈阳性时，科学家们更加怀疑他们正在观察红细胞。测试还发现了胶原蛋白的氨基酸组成部分的痕迹，胶原蛋白是结缔组织和其他组织中的关键蛋白质。
如果这些结构确实是红细胞化石，正如研究人员所说，这就提出了它们如何保存的问题。格赖斯表示，一种叫做黑锰矿的锰化合物形成于血细胞内部和周围，可能在血细胞石化之前稳定它们，从而起到了帮助作用。她补充说，同样的过程可能有助于保存氨基酸。该研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。
这项工作已经引发了争论。美国北卡罗来纳州立大学的玛丽·施韦策教授在恐龙化石中发现了血管和软组织的残留物，但她并不相信格赖斯和她的同事们已经发现了红细胞。她怀疑的原因之一是恐龙的红细胞应该有一个“核凸起”，使它们的两侧看起来像圆顶。格赖斯发现的结构是凹面的，这表明它们可能是别的东西。
施韦策对骨骼中血红素和胶原氨基酸的发现更加信服，并表示从保存完好的化石中可以学到更多东西。施韦策补充道：“古生物学中的传统观点认为，所有内源有机物都会在一百万年或更短的时间内消失，这种观点经常受到挑战，而且随着古生物学标本的技术方法得到更广泛的应用，这种挑战将继续存在。”
该研究提出的另一个问题是世界各地的化石收藏中可能潜藏着哪些其他生物材料。对此，格赖斯敦促要极其谨慎，并补充说，她的研究并不意味着蛋白质或 DNA 等大型生物分子存在于古代化石中。 “任何非凡的主张都需要非凡的分析证据，”她说。 “我们的目的不是寻找侏罗纪公园的 DNA，而是确定深层时间可以保存多少真实的分子信息。”
“真正令人兴奋的暗示是，非凡的分子信息可能已经存在于世界各地的博物馆藏品中，等待我们对古老化石提出新的问题，”她补充道。

title_en: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
title_zh: 调查人员称，佛罗里达州致命飞机失事前飞机可能已解体
summary: The National Transportation Safety Board also believes weather could have been a factor in the crash, but warns it is too early to determine the cause.
summary_zh: 美国国家运输安全委员会也认为天气可能是造成事故的一个因素，但警告说现在确定原因还为时过早
body_en: The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) says it will investigate whether parts of a jet that crashed in Florida broke off before it nose-dived and exploded, killing all nine people on board.
The Learjet 60, which was travelling from Austin, Texas to the Bahamas on Sunday, crashed on a street nine miles (14 km) from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort.
A tech entrepreneur and his young family, as well as the 20-year-old copilot, were among those who died.
The NTSB said on Monday that it would also investigate to what extent ice and turbulence may have been contributing factors.
It confirmed that, after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbulence.
"We are picking up precipitation, requesting to climb to 37,000 feet if able," the crew said.
NTSB member Tom Chapman said that less than 30 seconds later, the plane began to descend and the crew issued a mayday call.
The transmission then became "unintelligible", he said, adding that: "Sadly, all aboard were lost."
The NTSB said that ice and turbulence were factors in the crash but that determining its probable cause will be a "lengthy investigatory process".
Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time.
Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.
As part of the investigation, the NTSB is working with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), representatives from Learjet as well as meteorologists and air traffic control experts.
Recovering the wreckage from the crater on the roadway will be a "daunting challenge", said Timothy Monville, an air safety investigator with the safety board.
Flight analysis indicates the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.

In air traffic control audio, a crew member can be heard declaring an emergency, shouting "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".
About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last remark from the cockpit appears to be "we're out of time".

The seven people killed who were travelling as passengers were identified in a joint statement from their families as tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, and their two children - Emma and Charlie - as well as Rachael Reed, Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina.
The pilot was named in media reports as Jeffery Gregory, while Nathalia Filgueiras, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, was reported to be the copilot.
As well as those killed, one man on the ground sustained a leg injury when the plane nosedived onto the street.
The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said the crash happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road lined with businesses and restaurants.
body_zh: 美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）表示，将调查一架在佛罗里达州坠毁的飞机在俯冲并爆炸之前是否有部件断裂，导致机上九人全部遇难。
周日，这架里尔 60 型飞机从德克萨斯州奥斯汀飞往巴哈马，在距离唐纳德·特朗普总统的海湖庄园度假村 9 英里（14 公里）的街道上坠毁。
死者包括一名科技企业家和他年轻的家人，以及 20 岁的副驾驶。
美国国家运输安全委员会周一表示，还将调查冰和湍流在多大程度上可能是促成因素。
它证实，飞机从奥斯汀起飞后，机组人员向空中交通管制中心报告说，他们遇到了结冰和中度湍流。
“我们正在收集降水，如果可能的话，我们请求爬升到 37,000 英尺，”机组人员说。
NTSB成员汤姆·查普曼表示，不到30秒后，飞机开始下降，机组人员发出求救信号。
他说，传输信息随后变得“难以理解”，并补充道：“可悲的是，船上所有人都失踪了。”
美国国家运输安全委员会表示，冰和湍流是导致坠机的因素，但确定其可能的原因将是一个“漫长的调查过程”。
据报道，当时该地区有雷暴。
官员们还在试图查明坠机时机上是否有驾驶舱录音机以及是否可以恢复。
作为调查的一部分，国家运输安全委员会正在与美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA)、里尔喷气机公司的代表以及气象学家和空中交通管制专家合作。
安全委员会的航空安全调查员蒂莫西·蒙维尔表示，从道路上的弹坑中回收残骸将是一项“艰巨的挑战”。
飞行分析表明，这架飞机在坠毁前以每秒数百英尺的速度垂直下降。
在空中交通管制音频中，可以听到一名机组人员宣布紧急情况，大喊“我们处于每分钟下降 20,000 英尺的超速状态”，然后又说“我们将坠落到地面”。
在最初的求救消息发布后大约 35 秒，驾驶舱内的最后一句话似乎是“我们没时间了”。
在一份来自家人的联合声明中，遇难的七名乘客被确认为科技企业家亚当·罗宾逊、他的妻子海伦·夏普、他们的两个孩子艾玛和查理，以及瑞秋·里德、查米·费尔和安妮塔·玛丽亚·塞蒂娜。
媒体报道中，这名飞行员的名字是杰弗里·格雷戈里 (Jeffery Gregory)，而副驾驶则是娜塔莉亚·菲尔盖拉斯 (Nathalia Filgueiras)，她在 17 岁时获得了飞行员执照。
飞机俯冲到街道上时，除了遇难者外，地面上的一名男子腿部受伤。
棕榈滩县治安官办公室表示，事故发生在军事步道上，这是一条六车道的道路，两旁都是企业和餐馆。

title_en: War, tariffs and China: What the US midterms mean for the Asia-Pacific
title_zh: 战争、关税与中国：美国中期选举对亚太地区意味着什么
summary: Hit hard by Trump's tariffs and the war on Iran, countries in the Asia-Pacific want 'enormous changes' in US policies.
summary_zh: 受到特朗普关税和对伊朗战争的沉重打击，亚太国家希望美国政策发生“巨大改变”。
body_en: Share War, tariffs and China: What the US midterms mean for the Asia-Pacific on social media
Xi urges diplomacy on Iran as Oman’s sultan makes historic visit to China

Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia – Across the Asia-Pacific region, governments and businesses reeling from the energy shock of the United States and Israel’s war on Iran are watching Tuesday’s US midterm elections closely.

Many want to see “enormous changes” during the rest of President Donald Trump’s term, analysts say, from the war on Iran to his policies on trade and tariffs. But few expect that to happen, even with the Democrats poised to take the House of Representatives, and potentially the Senate, from Trump’s Republican Party.

“Of course, everybody is watching,” said Steven Okun, a trade specialist and the chief executive of APAC Advisors, a Singapore-based consulting firm. “It’s great political theatre.”

Outside the Middle East, no region has been hit harder by the war on Iran than the Asia-Pacific. Before the start of the conflict in January, the region took in most of the Gulf oil and gas that passed through the Strait of Hormuz.
When Iran closed the chokepoint in response to the US and Israel’s strikes, much of the region was left facing shortages .

The Philippines, which relies on the Gulf for more than 90 percent of its crude oil imports, has been under a national energy emergency since March. Soaring fuel costs have drained the foreign exchange reserves of the region’s poorest economies – Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and East Timor, according to the Institute of Southeast Asian Studies (ISEAS)-Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore. Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam have also spent heavily on fuel subsidies to shield consumers, it said.
Public opinion in the Asia-Pacific region remains firmly opposed to the war, but Okun said a Democratic-controlled US Congress was unlikely to force Trump to end the eight-month conflict.

“With Iran, I don’t see [a Democrat-controlled Congress] having much change at all, other than the fact that the war will be investigated and there will be oversight hearings,” Okun told Al Jazeera. “We might even see an impeachment of the secretary of defence, but it doesn’t change the overall impact of the war.”

Under the US Constitution, Congress holds the power to formally declare war, but Trump has claimed the attacks on Iran were in self-defence and has so far ignored congressional resolutions directing him to withdraw US forces from hostilities. If a Democrat-controlled Congress passes legislation restricting military operations or cutting funding for them, Trump can veto it. Overriding a veto requires a two-thirds majority in both chambers, which Democrats are almost certain to fall short of.
On trade and tariffs, too, analysts see little room for Congress to rein in Trump.

The US president rattled global markets last year when he imposed “reciprocal” tariffs of 10 percent to 50 percent on some 90 countries, with the aim of shrinking the US trade deficit. Asia was again hit harder than most. Cambodia faced a 49 percent tariff and Laos 48 percent. Vietnam was slapped with 46 percent and Myanmar 45 percent.

After the Supreme Court struck down those tariffs in February, the Trump administration turned to other tools . In July, it imposed tariffs of 10 percent and 12.5 percent on goods from 60 trading partners, accusing them of failing to stop imports made with forced labour . In Asia, the list includes China, Japan, South Korea and seven Southeast Asian nations – Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

“In some ways, the new Congress is not going to matter to the Asia Pacific because it’s not going to affect trade policy,” Okun said. “Congress cannot change that … Tariffs don’t change. The war doesn’t change.”

Stephen Olson, a visiting fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, argued in a recent essay that a “strong rebuke of ‘Trumpism’” at the polls could embolden a pro-free-trade wing of the Republican Party that has been “intimidated into standing down during the Trump presidency”.

That, Olson wrote, offers “a glimmer of hope” for Southeast Asian countries that depend on the US market. A Democratic-controlled Congress, he said, could also push for carve-outs and exceptions that would give the region’s exporters “a modicum of relief”. But any deeper shift in US trade policy, he added, will have to wait for the 2028 presidential election.
body_zh: 在社交媒体上分享战争、关税和中国：美国中期选举对亚太地区意味着什么
阿曼苏丹对中国进行历史性访问，习近平敦促对伊朗采取外交行动
马来西亚吉隆坡 — — 在整个亚太地区，受到美国能源冲击和以色列对伊朗战争影响的政府和企业正在密切关注周二的美国中期选举。
分析人士表示，许多人希望看到唐纳德·特朗普总统在剩余任期内发生“巨大变化”，从对伊朗的战争到他的贸易和关税政策。但很少有人预计这种情况会发生，即使民主党准备从特朗普领导的共和党手中夺取众议院席位，甚至可能夺取参议院席位。

list 2 of 3 随着家庭账单激增，美国石油公司如何从伊朗战争中获利 1,300 亿美元

“当然，每个人都在关注，”新加坡咨询公司 APAC Advisors 的贸易专家兼首席执行官史蒂文·奥肯 (Steven Okun) 表示。 “这是一场伟大的政治戏剧。”
在中东以外，没有哪个地区比亚太地区受到伊朗战争的打击更严重。在一月份冲突爆发之前，该地区吸收了大部分通过霍尔木兹海峡的海湾石油和天然气。
当伊朗因美国和以色列的袭击而关闭这一咽喉要道时，该地区大部分地区都面临着物资短缺。
菲律宾90%以上的原油进口依赖海湾地区，自3月份以来一直处于国家能源紧急状态。新加坡尤索夫伊萨东南亚研究所称，不断飙升的燃料成本耗尽了该地区最贫穷经济体——柬埔寨、老挝、缅甸和东帝汶的外汇储备。报告称，印度尼西亚、马来西亚、泰国和越南也投入巨资进行燃料补贴以保护消费者。
亚太地区的舆论仍然坚决反对这场战争，但奥肯表示，民主党控制的美国国会不太可能迫使特朗普结束长达八个月的冲突。
奥肯告诉半岛电视台：“对于伊朗，我认为（民主党控制的国会）根本不会有太大改变，除了将对战争进行调查并举行监督听证会之外。” “我们甚至可能会看到国防部长被弹劾，但这并不能改变战争的整体影响。”
根据美国宪法，国会拥有正式宣战的权力，但特朗普声称对伊朗的袭击是出于自卫，并且迄今为止无视国会指示他从敌对行动中撤军的决议。如果民主党控制的国会通过限制军事行动或削减军事行动经费的立法，特朗普可以否决。推翻否决权需要在参众两院获得三分之二多数，而民主党几乎肯定达不到这一点。
在贸易和关税方面，分析人士也认为国会限制特朗普的空间很小。
去年，美国总统为了缩小美国的贸易逆差，对约 90 个国家征收 10% 至 50% 的“互惠”关税，震惊了全球市场。亚洲再次受到比大多数国家更严重的打击。柬埔寨面临 49% 的关税，老挝则面临 48% 的关税。越南占 46%，缅甸占 45%。
在最高法院二月份推翻这些关税后，特朗普政府转向了其他工具。 7月，中国对来自60个贸易伙伴的商品征收10%和12.5%的关税，指责它们未能阻止强迫劳动进口。在亚洲，名单包括中国、日本、韩国和七个东南亚国家——柬埔寨、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾、新加坡、泰国和越南。
“在某些方面，新国会对亚太地区并不重要，因为它不会影响贸易政策，”奥肯说。 “国会无法改变这一点……关税不会改变。战争不会改变。”
尤索夫伊萨东南亚研究所的客座研究员史蒂芬·奥尔森在最近的一篇文章中指出，民意调查中“对‘特朗普主义’的强烈谴责”可能会让共和党中支持自由贸易的派系“在特朗普担任总统期间被恐吓下台”。
奥尔森写道，这为依赖美国市场的东南亚国家带来了“一线希望”。他说，民主党控制的国会还可以推动例外和例外，这将为该地区的出口商带来“一点缓解”。但他补充说，美国贸易政策的任何更深层次转变都必须等到 2028 年总统大选。

title_en: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court
title_zh: 对澳大利亚社交媒体禁令的法律挑战将在高等法院启动
summary: A rights group will argue the world-leading policy robs under-16s of their right to free communication.
summary_zh: 一个权利组织将辩称，这项世界领先的政策剥夺了 16 岁以下青少年自由交流的权利。
body_en: Image source, Supplied: Digital Freedom Project
Two days of hearings on a challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children will begin at the country's highest court on Tuesday.

In a major test of the world-leading policy, a digital rights group will argue that the ban for under-16s robs children of their right to free communication. A separate challenge launched by platform Reddit will be jointly heard.
Introduced last December, the ban is a key part of sweeping changes the Australian government has spearheaded in recent years on online safety.
Supporters say the ban protects children from harmful content but critics say it is too blunt an instrument and efforts should focus on improving online safety.

The constitutional challenge in Australia's High Court was filed by the Digital Freedom Project a few weeks before the ban started on 10 December last year. The group is lead by New South Wales parliamentarian John Ruddick.
Two teens who originally spearheaded the case , Noah Jones and Macy Neyland, have since withdrawn as plaintiffs though Jones is still expected to attend Tuesday's hearing.
Speaking about the legal challenge last November, Jones told the BBC that there were bad things online but a blanket ban for under-16s was not the right answer.
"We shouldn't be using the resources and money of these social media platforms to try to avoid fines from our government," he said.
"They should be using this money and resources to try to get rid of the predators and harmful content out there."
Reddit also launched a High Court challenge to the ban, arguing the policy has serious implications for privacy and political rights.
The company said it shared Australia's goal of protecting young people online "but there are better and more effective ways" than a ban.
"As we challenge this law in court, we'll continue to comply with it and advocate for more effective youth safety measures," said Reddit's chief communications officer Adam Collins.
Communications Minister Anika Wells last year said the government would not be "intimidated by legal threats."
"We will not be intimidated by big tech. On behalf of Australian parents, we will stand firm," she said last November.

Under the ban, ten platforms - Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Snapchat, X, Kick, Threads and Twitch - must take "reasonable steps" to ensure no one under 16 years old can access its site.
Platforms risk fines of up to A$99m (US$70m, £52m) for serious or repeated breaches, but since the ban started, no company has been fined.
WhatsApp and online gaming sites like Roblox and Discord were not included in the ban, nor were educational platforms like YouTube Kids and Google Classroom.
In the first few days of the ban, Meta - which owns three of the banned platforms - said it had closed about half a million accounts.

Some children said they were booted off their accounts in the days before and when the ban started - but many have said they were able to easily circumvent the age checks which included uploading credit card details, photo IDs or a selfie.
body_zh: 图片来源，提供：数字自由项目
澳大利亚最高法院将于周二开始为期两天的听证会，审理澳大利亚具有里程碑意义的儿童社交媒体禁令的挑战。
在对世界领先政策的重大考验中，一个数字权利组织将辩称，针对 16 岁以下儿童的禁令剥夺了儿童自由交流的权利。 Reddit 平台发起的另一项挑战将联合审理。
该禁令于去年 12 月推出，是澳大利亚政府近年来在网络安全方面带头进行的全面变革的关键部分。
支持者表示，该禁令可以保护儿童免受有害内容的侵害，但批评者表示，该禁令过于生硬，应集中精力提高网络安全。
去年 12 月 10 日禁令开始实施前几周，数字自由项目向澳大利亚高等法院提出了宪法质疑。该组织由新南威尔士州议员约翰·鲁迪克领导。
最初牵头此案的两名青少年诺亚·琼斯（Noah Jones）和梅西·内兰（Macy Neyland）现已退出原告身份，但预计琼斯仍将出席周二的听证会。
谈到去年 11 月的法律挑战时，琼斯告诉 BBC，网上有不好的事情，但全面禁止 16 岁以下青少年并不是正确的答案。
“我们不应该利用这些社交媒体平台的资源和金钱来试图避免政府的罚款，”他说。
“他们应该利用这些资金和资源来消除掠夺者和有害内容。”
Reddit 还向高等法院发起对该禁令的挑战，认为该政策对隐私和政治权利产生严重影响。
该公司表示，它与澳大利亚有共同的目标，即保护年轻人上网，“但有比禁令更好、更有效的方法”。
Reddit 首席通讯官 Adam Collins 表示：“当我们在法庭上质疑这项法律时，我们将继续遵守该法律，并倡导采取更有效的青少年安全措施。”
通讯部长阿尼卡·威尔斯去年表示，政府不会“被法律威胁吓倒”。
“我们不会被大型科技吓倒。代表澳大利亚家长，我们将坚定立场，”她去年11月表示。
根据该禁令，Facebook、Instagram、TikTok、YouTube、Reddit、Snapchat、X、Kick、Threads 和 Twitch 等 10 个平台必须采取“合理措施”，确保 16 岁以下的任何人都无法访问其网站。
对于严重或反复违规的平台，可能面临高达 9900 万澳元（7000 万美元，5200 万英镑）的罚款，但自禁令开始以来，没有一家公司被罚款。
WhatsApp 以及 Roblox 和 Discord 等在线游戏网站不包括在禁令范围内，YouTube Kids 和 Google Classroom 等教育平台也不包括在禁令范围内。
拥有三个被禁平台的 Meta 表示，在禁令实施的最初几天，它已经关闭了大约 50 万个账户。
一些孩子表示，他们在禁令开始前几天和禁令开始时就被从账户中删除了，但许多人表示，他们能够轻松绕过年龄检查，其中包括上传信用卡详细信息、带照片的身份证件或自拍照。

Ahead of the United States midterm elections , President Donald Trump’s job approval rating continues to sit near a record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.
Some 32 percent of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the presidency, 1 percentage point above his rating two weeks ago.

list 2 of 3 How the president’s party has fared in every US midterm election since 1946
list 3 of 3 Trump, Vance campaign with candidates on last day before US midterms

Meanwhile, the Republican Party continues to be unpopular among those polled: When asked whether they would vote for a generic Democrat or Republican candidate, 46 percent of respondents preferred Democrats compared with 38 percent preferring Republicans.

Trump himself is not on the ballot, but he has repeatedly told his supporters to vote as if they are voting for him. If the Republican Party loses control of the US Congress, Trump has warned, Democrats may seek to impeach him for a third time.

Trump’s approval rating has dropped steadily, polls suggest, especially since the launch of the US-Israel war on Iran on February 28. The conflict has driven up petrol and diesel prices and has had secondary effects for US consumers worried about inflation and the economy.

The president embarked on a nearly monthlong campaign blitz ahead of the November 3 midterms in an effort to shore up support for Republican candidates, who are trying to retain control of the US House of Representatives and Senate.

Trump wrapped up his campaigning on Monday afternoon with a rally in Washington, DC, at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The president has devoted significant attention to the site as part of his attempt to renovate the capital. The job ran months late and cost more than 10 times its original estimate, with a special liner for the pool that Trump touted peeling away soon after it was installed.

“It was a work of art that never worked, but now it will work,” Trump said at the rally. He spent much of his speech on his renovation plans for the city, including a “Triumphal Arch”, which is facing legal challenges .
Trump seemed to acknowledge on Monday that his campaigning might not deliver the results he wants for his party, but said this was the political norm for midterm elections.
“For some reason, the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms,” Trump said. “But we gave this a very strong shot.”

title_en: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
title_zh: 联合国在有争议的西撒哈拉的维和任务结束35年后
summary: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.
summary_zh: 联合国在有争议的西撒哈拉地区执行的长期维和任务在执行了 35 年后于周日结束。曾经被西班牙统治过，有人声称
body_en: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
FILE - A Sahrawi refugee boy stands in the shadow in the Boujdour refugee camp, Oct. 11, 2021. Bernat Armangue/AP hide caption

CASABLANCA, Morocco — The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years, as a result of a U.S.-Russia standoff at U.N. headquarters over the territory's future.

The end of the mission raises concerns about stability in the region. Rich in minerals and fisheries, Western Sahara is a vast desert territory roughly the size of Colorado along Africa's northwestern Atlantic coast. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

"This 1 November 2026 marks the start of the liquidation period," Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for the U.N. secretary general, said in a statement. "A smaller team reporting to the United Nations' Department of Operational Support will oversee the orderly transportation of assets belonging to troop-contributing countries to their respective nations, and the appropriate disposal of equipment belonging to the United Nations.''

The mission had been repeatedly extended since it was established in 1991. In the U.N. Security Council on Friday, Russia vetoed a draft U.S. resolution that would have supported Morocco's demand for sovereignty over Western Sahara and ended the peacekeeping mission next year.
What really happened in Ceuta? Why we may never find out
Then a rival Russian resolution to extend the mission was voted down. The disagreement led to an abrupt end of the force's mandate.
Morocco's royal palace welcomed the non-renewal of the mission. It called it an "instrument to internationalize the dispute.''

The Polisario Front, backed by Algeria, called it "an unacceptable decision.'' The Algerian foreign ministry said it profoundly regrets the non-renewal of the mandate and criticized what it called the ''excessive bias'' of the U.S. draft resolution.
Western Sahara is Africa's longest territorial dispute

The U.N. classifies Western Sahara as a "non-self-governing territory," while critics of Morocco's control describe it as Africa's last colony. Morocco administers nearly all of the disputed territory, except for a narrow strip known as the "free zone" that lies east of a Moroccan-built sand wall.
After Morocco annexed it in 1975, the dispute escalated into an armed conflict that lasted more than 15 years and claimed more than 16,000 lives on both sides, according to the French Senate.

Bringing Western Sahara under its full sovereignty has been a central objective of Morocco's foreign policy for decades. Rabat, which has secured the backing of a growing number of Western capitals, including Washington, Paris and London, refers to the territory as its southern provinces. The dispute has become a defining feature of Morocco's diplomacy, with the kingdom often measuring its relations with other countries by their position on the issue.

The Polisario Front seeks independence for the territory, which it considers the homeland of the Indigenous Sahrawi people. Operating from refugee camps in the Algerian city of Tindouf, the movement aims to establish an independent Sahrawi Republic. Mainly backed by Algeria, Russia and South Africa, the Polisario has seen its international support dwindle in recent years.
The expired mission was established to monitor a referendum
A U.N.-brokered cease-fire took effect in 1991. The agreement also paved the way for the creation of the U.N. Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO.

The settlement plan provided for a referendum on self-determination, with independence among the options. But the vote never materialized. Morocco wanted the voter list to include Sahrawis living in the territory it controls, while the Polisario objected, arguing that their inclusion would tilt the outcome toward integration with Morocco. The movement insisted on using Spain's colonial census to determine voter eligibility.
Spain's Pedro Sánchez was a hero of migrants. After Ceuta, he faces his biggest challenge

Twenty MINURSO personnel lost their lives in the mission. The U.N. force was authorized to have 534 personnel, and its 2026-2027 budget was more than $62 million. The top military contributors to the force were Egypt, Ghana and Pakistan.
body_zh: 联合国在有争议的西撒哈拉的维和任务结束35年后
文件 - 2021 年 10 月 11 日，一名撒哈拉难民男孩站在布支杜尔难民营的阴影中。Bernat Armangue/美联社隐藏标题栏
摩洛哥卡萨布兰卡——由于美俄在联合国总部围绕该领土的未来陷入对峙，联合国在有争议的西撒哈拉地区执行的长期维和任务在执行了 35 年后于周日停止行动。
任务的结束引发了对该地区稳定的担忧。西撒哈拉拥有丰富的矿产和渔业资源，是非洲西北大西洋沿岸一片广阔的沙漠地区，面积大约相当于科罗拉多州的大小。曾经由西班牙统治，摩洛哥和支持独立的波利萨里奥阵线均声称拥有主权。
联合国秘书长发言人斯特凡·杜雅里克 (Stéphane Dujarric) 在一份声明中表示：“2026 年 11 月 1 日标志着清理期的开始。” “向联合国行动支持部报告的一个较小的团队将监督部队派遣国的资产有序运输到各自国家，以及联合国设备的适当处置。”
自1991年成立以来，该任务已多次延长。周五，俄罗斯在联合国安理会否决了美国一项支持摩洛哥对西撒哈拉主权要求的决议草案，并于明年结束了维和任务。
休达到底发生了什么？为什么我们可能永远不会发现
随后，俄罗斯一项延长任务期限的竞争对手决议被否决。这一分歧导致该部队的任务突然终止。
摩洛哥王宫对不再延长任务期限表示欢迎。它称其为“使争端国际化的工具。”
阿尔及利亚支持的波利萨里奥阵线称这是“一个不可接受的决定”。阿尔及利亚外交部表示，对不延长授权深感遗憾，并批评美国决议草案“过度偏见”。
西撒哈拉是非洲最长的领土争端
联合国将西撒哈拉列为“非自治领土”，而摩洛哥控制的批评者则将其描述为非洲最后的殖民地。摩洛哥管理着几乎所有有争议的领土，除了位于摩洛哥建造的沙墙以东的一条被称为“自由区”的狭长地带。
据法国参议院称，摩洛哥于 1975 年吞并该国后，争端升级为武装冲突，持续了 15 年多，并夺走了双方 16,000 多人的生命。
几十年来，将西撒哈拉置于其完全主权之下一直是摩洛哥外交政策的核心目标。拉巴特已经获得了越来越多西方国家首都的支持，包括华盛顿、巴黎和伦敦，该地区将其称为南部省份。这一争端已成为摩洛哥外交的一个决定性特征，该王国经常根据其他国家在该问题上的立场来衡量其与其他国家的关系。
波利萨里奥阵线寻求该地区的独立，它认为该地区是撒哈拉原住民的家园。该运动在阿尔及利亚廷杜夫市的难民营开展活动，旨在建立一个独立的撒哈拉共和国。波利萨里奥主要得到阿尔及利亚、俄罗斯和南非的支持，近年来其国际支持不断减少。
已过期的特派团是为了监测公投而设立的
联合国斡旋的停火于 1991 年生效。该协议还为创建联合国西撒哈拉全民投票特派团（即 MINURSO）铺平了道路。
解决计划规定就自决进行全民公投，其中包括独立性选项。但投票从未实现。摩洛哥希望选民名单中包括居住在其控制领土上的撒哈拉人，而波利萨里奥党则表示反对，认为将他们纳入选民名单将使结果倾向于与摩洛哥一体化。该运动坚持利用西班牙殖民地人口普查来确定选民资格。
西班牙的佩德罗·桑切斯是移民英雄。休达之后，他面临最大的挑战
20 名西撒特派团人员在任务中丧生。联合国部队被授权拥有 534 名人员，2026-2027 年预算超过 6200 万美元。该部队的最大军事派遣国是埃及、加纳和巴基斯坦。

title_en: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
title_zh: 男子因从南非总统拥有的农场偷窃现金而被判有罪
summary: The case, part of the "Farmgate" scandal, has left President Cyril Ramaphosa mired in an impeachment saga.
summary_zh: 该案是“农场门”丑闻的一部分，使总统西里尔·拉马福萨陷入弹劾传奇。
body_en: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president - BBC News

A court in South Africa has found a man guilty of stealing more than $500,000 (£372,822) in cash from a farm owned by South African president Cyril Ramaphosa, in a case that mired the head of state in an impeachment saga.
Imanuwela David was found guilty of theft on Monday, as well as conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal at Phala Phala farm in the Limpopo province in 2020.
Froliana Joseph, a cleaner at the property, was also found guilty of conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal.
Her brother, Ndilinasho Joseph, was acquitted on all charges.

David was accused of breaking into the cattle farm in February 2020 and taking $580,000 (£432,000) in cash from a sofa on the property. David then went on a spending spree, buying a range of cars including three Mercedes - among them one for his girlfriend - a Porsche, two Volkswagens as well as diamond-encrusted Rolex watches and a house.

David told the court he had made the money through businesses including diamonds and Bitcoin, claims the court rejected. The court also found that David was the only one of the two convicted who had any of the stolen cash in his bank account.
Pre-sentencing will take place on 13 November.
There have been many twists and turns in what is known as the Farmgate scandal.

The theft was largely unknown until 2022 when it was brought to light by Arthur Fraser, South Africa's former intelligence chief and an ally for the former president Jacob Zuma, when he claimed that Ramaphosa hid the theft from the police and tax authorities.
Ramaphosa admitted the theft took place but denied any wrongdoing.
An independent panel that same year found Ramaphosa could have questions to answer over the burglary. MPs voted against establishing an impeachment inquiry.

In May this year, the constitutional court ruled that parliament had acted unlawfully by shelving the panel's report, and in July Ramaphosa blocked the parliamentary inquiry through a provincial court.
The cash-in-the-sofa saga that just won't go away for South Africa's president
body_zh: 男子因从南非总统拥有的农场偷窃现金而被判有罪 -_澳门赌博平台
南非一家法院判定一名男子从南非总统西里尔·拉马福萨 (Cyril Ramaphosa) 拥有的农场盗窃超过 50 万美元（合 372,822 英镑）现金，此案使国家元首陷入弹劾传奇。
周一，伊马努韦拉·大卫 (Imanuwela David) 被判犯有盗窃罪，并于 2020 年在林波波省的 Phala Phala 农场合谋入室盗窃。
该物业的清洁工弗洛丽安娜·约瑟夫 (Froliana Joseph) 也被判犯有串谋入室盗窃罪。
她的兄弟恩迪利纳肖·约瑟夫 (Ndilinasho Joseph) 所有指控均被无罪释放。
大卫被指控于 2020 年 2 月闯入养牛场，并从农场的沙发上拿走了 580,000 美元（432,000 英镑）现金。随后，大卫开始疯狂消费，购买了一系列汽车，包括三辆奔驰（其中一辆是给他女朋友的）、一辆保时捷、两辆大众汽车以及镶钻劳力士手表和一栋房子。
大卫告诉法庭，他是通过钻石和比特币等业务赚到钱的，但法庭驳回了这一说法。法院还发现，大卫是两名被定罪者中唯一一个在银行账户中存有被盗现金的人。
预判将于 11 月 13 日进行。
所谓的“农场门”丑闻经历了许多曲折。
这起盗窃案直到 2022 年才被南非前情报局长、前总统雅各布·祖马的盟友阿瑟·弗雷泽曝光，当时他声称拉马福萨向警方和税务机关隐瞒了这起盗窃案。
拉马福萨承认发生了盗窃事件，但否认有任何不当行为。
同年，一个独立小组发现拉马福萨可能对入室盗窃案有疑问需要回答。议员们投票反对建立弹劾调查。
今年5月，宪法法院裁定议会搁置该小组报告的行为非法，7月拉马福萨通过省法院阻止了议会调查。

title_en: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
title_zh: 特朗普将把卢旺达和南非从美国贸易协定中删除
summary: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.
summary_zh: 此举是在卢旺达国防部受到美国财政部制裁后不到一周发生的。
body_en: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal - BBC News
US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027.
The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements.
He added that the Trump administration had additionally notified the two countries of the decision.
The Trump administration cited barriers to US trade and investment, as well as concerns over national security and foreign policy interests in the region.
In Rwanda's case, Washington also raised concerns about human rights, political pluralism, the rule of law and workers' rights.
The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by US Treasury for its alleged role in the armed rebellion in eastern DR Congo.
The US Treasury said Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 rebels in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training.
For South Africa, the US additionally pointed to corruption.
"The Trump administration is working to ensure our African partners take the necessary steps to meet the eligibility criteria," Greer said.
The announcement comes amid strained relations between Washington and both countries, with the proposed termination threatening their access to preferential trade arrangements with the US.
Last year, Trump accused South Africa of white genocide in a meeting with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the White House and launched a US refugee pathway for Afrikaners.
US Ambassador to South Africa Leo Brent Bozell III said it was regrettable that South African policies led to its termination from Agoa.
"This was a predictable and preventable outcome resulting from the rejection by South Africa's government of real concerns raised by the US," he wrote on X.
body_zh: 特朗普将把卢旺达和南非从美国贸易协定中删除 -_澳门赌博平台
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普已通知国会，他打算从 2027 年 1 月 1 日起将南非和卢旺达从优惠贸易计划中删除。
《非洲增长与机会法案》(Agoa) 允许符合条件的非洲国家向美国免税出口数千种产品。
美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔在一份声明中表示，年度审查发现两国的做法不符合该计划的资格要求。
他补充说，特朗普政府还向两国通报了这一决定。
特朗普政府列举了美国贸易和投资的障碍，以及对该地区国家安全和外交政策利益的担忧。
在卢旺达事件中，华盛顿还对人权、政治多元化、法治和工人权利表示担忧。
就在卢旺达国防部因涉嫌参与刚果民主共和国东部武装叛乱而受到美国财政部制裁后不到一周。
美国财政部表示，卢旺达国防部指示数千名士兵在刚果民主共和国东部与“3·23”运动叛军并肩作战，提供武器、装备、后勤和培训。
对于南非，美国还指出了腐败问题。
格里尔说：“特朗普政府正在努力确保我们的非洲合作伙伴采取必要措施来满足资格标准。”
这一消息是在华盛顿与两国关系紧张之际做出的，拟议的终止威胁到两国与美国享受优惠贸易安排的机会。
去年，特朗普在白宫与西里尔·拉马福萨总统会面时指责南非进行白人种族灭绝，并为南非荷兰语人启动了美国难民通道。
美国驻南非大使利奥·布伦特·博泽尔三世表示，令人遗憾的是，南非的政策导致其终止加入Agoa。
他在 X 上写道：“这是一个可以预见、可以预防的结果，因为南非政府拒绝接受美国提出的真正关切。”

body_en: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Efrat Shapira Rosenberg, Israeli Radio/TV Host, Columnist, Podcaster and Educator. title_en: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
title_zh: 英国“激烈”奴隶制赔偿不应列入英联邦峰会议程
summary: British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leade
summary_zh: 英国首相现已同意就赔偿性司法进行结构化对话，但该问题仍不在 Chogm 的正式议程中 英国官员报告
body_en: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda

British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.

Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.

Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.

“My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.

“They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”

Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.

“Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.

He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”

Gonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.
He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”

An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.
“Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”
‘We want a full apology for slavery’: Commonwealth at a crossroads as king heads to the Caribbean

Prof Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.
On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology .

Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.
Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.
body_zh: 英国“激烈”奴隶制赔偿不应列入英联邦峰会议程
英国首相现已同意就赔偿性司法进行结构化对话，但该问题仍不在乔格姆的正式议程中
据报道，英国官员坚称，关于奴隶制赔偿的讨论不应列入安提瓜和巴布达英联邦领导人峰会的议程，据加勒比一位重要政治人物称，英国官员甚至警告称，如果该主题被正式纳入，安迪·伯纳姆将不会出席会议。
圣文森特和格林纳丁斯前总理、修复正义运动“修复运动”的高级人物拉尔夫·贡萨尔维斯对英国决定就赔偿问题进行结构化对话表示欢迎，但他表示，英国在对话中“又踢又叫”。
目前，奴隶制赔偿问题并未列入周日召开的英联邦政府首脑（Chogm）峰会的正式议程。
贸易、气候适应力和金融、可持续债务、民主和对年轻人机会的投资是跨越非洲、亚洲、加勒比地区、美洲、太平洋和欧洲的 56 个国家集团的既定优先事项。
“我从知情人士那里得到的理解是，英国极力不把此事列入议程。英国官员——在这方面加拿大官员也加入了他们的行列——甚至提出了这样的可能性：如果此事列入议程，英国首相就不会去，”贡萨尔维斯告诉《卫报》。
“他们还开始散布印度不希望将其列入议程的谎言，但事实并非如此。印度非常支持 2026 年 3 月 25 日的联合国大会决议。所以他们散布了有关印度的虚假消息。”
贡萨尔维斯表示，加勒比国家的不懈努力，加上日益壮大的区域和全球赔偿运动，将赔偿正义推向了会议政治对话的核心。
“由于联合国发生的事情，由于非洲发生的事情，加勒比海地区发生的事情，以及英国国内、英国议会内部、英国工党内部、下议院和上议院正在开展的所有工作，这是一个你不能再回避的问题，”他说。
他补充道：“不将其正式列入议程的危险就是我们现在所看到的情况，每个能够预见的人，无论它是否正式列入议程，甚至在英联邦，当然还有务虚会上如何进行讨论的性质，都会被提出。”
贡萨尔维斯表示，虽然实际的结构化对话不太可能在乔姆举行，但预计当领导人在私人静修中会面时，将讨论对话的形式和细节。
他说：“英国政府，他们来了，又踢又叫地来到结构化对话的桌子上。但至少他们来了。”
FCDO 发言人表示：“我们断然拒绝这一完全不实的指控。英国本着善意进行这次对话，我们从未告诉任何其他 Chogm 成员什么不应该列入议程。
“我们在赔偿问题上的立场很明确，但本届政府尊重其他人按照自己的意愿提出问题的权利。”
“我们希望为奴隶制道歉”：国王前往加勒比海，英联邦正处于十字路口
加勒比共同体（Caricom）赔偿委员会主席希拉里·贝克尔斯（Hilary Beckles）爵士教授将这次会议描述为“赔偿的乔格姆”，并补充说，当英联邦领导人聚集在该地区时，赔偿正义是加勒比地区的“头等大事”。
周五，英国的立场发生了历史性转变，英国首相比任何一位前任都走得更远，同意进行结构化对话并考虑道歉。
尽管加勒比各国政府和活动家对伯纳姆在《卫报》专栏中宣布的消息表示欢迎，但很明显，就赔偿形式达成一致仍然是该地区的首要任务。
圭亚那总统伊尔法安·阿里对伯纳姆的声明表示欢迎，并呼吁英联邦小组委员会在未来 6 至 12 个月内制定对话细节。

title_en: What might Trump have planned for Iran following the midterm election?
title_zh: 中期选举后特朗普可能对伊朗有何计划？
summary: While the US midterms could open a window for diplomacy with Iran, they could also unleash a new military escalation. DW spoke with analysts to identify eight factors that could tip the balance toward war or peace.
summary_zh: 虽然美国中期选举可能打开与伊朗外交的窗口，但也可能引发新的军事升级。德国之声与分析师交谈以确定
body_en: The US Republican Party is entering the midterm elections with Donald Trump 's administration seemingly unable to either win or diplomatically resolve the Iran war . If the Republicans lose control of the US Congress , the administration will have to navigate an entirely different political landscape for the rest of Trump's second term, but the course of the war is not decided just in Washington — or in Tehran.

Seeking to identify key factors that could tip the balance towards war or peace in Iran , DW spoke with Omid Memarian of DAWN, a Washington-based think tank focused on reforming the US's Middle East policy; the Finland-based political scientist Leila Morovati; and Babak Rezaeedaryakenari, a professor of international relations at Leiden University in the Netherlands.
1. US midterms: Is Trump set for more scrutiny?

A Democratic victory would push Trump to focus more on domestic issues and would likely expose the financial costs of the war in the US Congress, Memarian told DW. However, Trump could continue limited strikes on Iran without formally declaring war.
Memarian said Trump would seek a way out that "saves face" after Tuesday's election.
With Trump, Memarian said, Iran is engaged in a "big gamble with someone who does not behave like a conventional politician." This increases the risk of renewed attacks.
How serious are Iran's new threats of retaliation?

Rezaeedaryakenari made a similar point: "The president has broad authority and freedom of action, especially in foreign policy and the conduct of military operations. A Republican defeat, even with increased pressure from Congress, doesn't necessarily stop new attacks."
2. Deadlock in Israel puts pressure on Netanyahu

Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock. Neither the coalition around incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , nor the camp supporting former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot managed to secure an outright majority.

Memarian said the political uncertainty could push Netanyahu to act on major decisions while he still wields power — making the transition period the "most fragile and dangerous" for renewed escalation.

A change of government in Israel would not fundamentally alter Israel's Iran policy , Memarian said. Netanyahu's main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, "may be more deferential to America" and coordinate more closely with Washington. But ties with Trump are personal, and Eisenkot "certainly won't be like Netanyahu, who could sell any plan or scenario to Trump."

Rezaeedaryakenari said Israel 's security concerns about Iran "are not limited to Netanyahu himself." A new government could change the timing of a confrontation and coordination with Washington, but the security establishment and ruling coalition would also shape the risk of an attack, he said.
Iran's nuclear program remains the biggest open issue between the governments, with the US rejecting the Iranian narrative that the program is meant only for civilian use .
But the two sides are also at odds on how the talks themselves should be set up, Memarian said.
"The US wants negotiations to start not only with a focus on Iran's nuclear program, but with concessions right at the outset," he said.
Iran seeks the lifting of sanctions and the release of frozen assets before nuclear talks begin. If the sides don't move closer, Memarian warns, the odds of a renewed war rise.
Until the sides agree on an agenda, Memarian said, they are likely to keep "climbing the ladder of tension."
body_zh: 美国共和党即将进入中期选举，唐纳德·特朗普政府似乎既无法赢得伊朗战争，也无法通过外交手段解决伊朗战争。如果共和党失去对美国国会的控制，特朗普政府将不得不在特朗普第二任期的剩余时间内应对完全不同的政治格局，但战争的进程不仅仅由华盛顿或德黑兰决定。
为了找出可能使伊朗局势走向战争还是和平的关键因素，德国之声采访了 DAWN 的奥米德·梅马里安 (Omid Memarian)。DAWN 是一家总部位于华盛顿的智库，致力于改革美国的中东政策。芬兰政治学家莱拉·莫洛瓦蒂 (Leila Morovati)；以及荷兰莱顿大学国际关系学教授巴巴克·雷扎埃达亚肯纳里 (Babak Rezaeedaryakenari)。
1. 美国中期选举：特朗普是否会受到更多审查？
梅马里安告诉德国之声，民主党的胜利将促使特朗普更加关注国内问题，并可能在美国国会暴露战争的财务成本。然而，特朗普可以在不正式宣战的情况下继续对伊朗进行有限打击。
梅马里安表示，特朗普将在周二大选后寻求“保全面子”的出路。
梅马里安说，伊朗正在与特朗普进行一场“与一个行为方式不像传统政治家的人的豪赌”。这增加了再次遭受攻击的风险。

雷扎埃达亚肯纳里也提出了类似的观点：“总统拥有广泛的权力和行动自由，特别是在外交政策和军事行动方面。即使国会压力加大，共和党的失败也不一定会阻止新的袭击。”
2、以色列僵局给内塔尼亚胡带来压力
以色列10月27日的选举陷入僵局。现任总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡周围的联盟和支持前以色列国防军主席加迪·艾森科特的阵营都未能获得绝对多数。
梅马里安表示，政治不确定性可能会促使内塔尼亚胡在仍掌握权力的情况下做出重大决定，从而使过渡期成为局势再次升级的“最脆弱和危险”的时期。
梅马里安说，以色列政府的更迭不会从根本上改变以色列的伊朗政策。内塔尼亚胡的主要竞争对手、前军事首长加迪·艾森科特“可能会更加尊重美国”，并与华盛顿进行更密切的协调。但与特朗普的关系是私人的，艾森科特“当然不会像内塔尼亚胡那样，可以向特朗普兜售任何计划或方案”。
雷扎伊达亚肯纳里表示，以色列对伊朗的安全担忧“不仅限于内塔尼亚胡本人”。他说，新政府可能会改变与华盛顿对抗和协调的时机，但安全机构和执政联盟也会影响袭击的风险。
伊朗核计划仍然是两国政府之间最大的公开问题，美国拒绝接受伊朗关于该计划仅供民用的说法。
但梅马里安表示，双方在如何安排谈判方面也存在分歧。
他说：“美国希望谈判开始时不仅要关注伊朗核计划，而且要从一开始就做出让步。”
伊朗寻求在核谈判开始前解除制裁并释放冻结的资产。梅马里安警告说，如果双方不进一步靠近，重新爆发战争的可能性就会上升。
梅马里安说，在双方就议程达成一致之前，他们可能会继续“攀登紧张局势”。
